subject: Request for runtime pipeline lab artifacts for RFP response
summary: External RFP asks for detailed runtime artifacts and lab evidence. Sales acknowledges and coordinates an internal runbook and artifacts deliverable; engineering provides kernel selection, raw logs, and benchmark CSVs with methodology notes.
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aperture-sys.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-10 08:12 PST
Subject: Request: runtime pipeline lab artifacts for RFP - Redwood

Rafael,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As part of Aperture's procurement RFP we need the following to validate performance claims in Section 4 (Latency & Throughput):

- Full list of microbenchmarks and the raw CSV outputs (p50/p90/p99) used to derive your published latency numbers.
- Kernel selection matrix and the decision logic you applied for different model families and sequence lengths.
- Raw run logs and the harness used (command lines, environment variables, container tags).
- Description of warmup/burn-in, cache-warm strategies (prefix/KV cache behavior).
- Hardware specification for the runs and any quantization profiles used.

We will treat these as confidential and they will be ingested into our evaluation lab (NDA in place). Target turnaround: by COB Wed 2026-12-16. If you can provide a short checklist and a single tarball of artifacts, that would help our automation.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Senior Procurement Manager | Aperture Systems

--
Attachment: rfp-exhibit-performance.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aperture-sys.com>
Cc: Ivy Chen <ivy.chen@aperture-sys.com>
Date: 2026-12-11 09:03 PST
Subject: Re: Request: runtime pipeline lab artifacts for RFP - Redwood

Sanjay / Ivy,

Appreciate the clear ask. We're assembling a focused artifact bundle and an annotated checklist so your team can ingest into the Aperture lab automation. High-level plan:

1) Deliverables (single tarball + checklist): kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx, runtime-benchmarks-2026-12-02.csv, burnin-log-2026-12-01.tar.gz, redwood-runtime-lab-notes.pdf.
2) Methodology note: sampling windows, warmup/burn-in policy, continuous batching settings, KV/prefix cache behavior and how it was measured.
3) Command lines and container image tags for reproducibility.

I copied our performance lead (Vivek) and PM (Marissa) to coordinate the exact artifact formats and to confirm timelines. Expect the first bundle by EOD Monday (2026-12-13). If you have a preferred file manifest format, send it over and we'll match it.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

--
Attachment: artifact-request-checklist.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-11 09:10 PST
Subject: Fwd: Request: runtime pipeline lab artifacts for RFP - Redwood

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Aperture's artifact list. They want a single tarball + checklist by COB 2026-12-13. Key asks are listed below; please confirm what we can deliver and any gaps.

Quoted message from Sanjay Rao:
> Rafael,
>
> As part of Aperture's procurement RFP we need the following to validate performance claims in Section 4 (Latency & Throughput):
>
> - Full list of microbenchmarks and the raw CSV outputs (p50/p90/p99) used to derive your published latency numbers.
> - Kernel selection matrix and the decision logic you applied for different model families and sequence lengths.
> - Raw run logs and the harness used (command lines, environment variables, container tags).
> - Description of warmup/burn-in, cache-warm strategies (prefix/KV cache behavior).
> - Hardware specification for the runs and any quantization profiles used.

Requested deliverables (from my note): kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx, runtime-benchmarks-2026-12-02.csv, burnin-log-2026-12-01.tar.gz, redwood-runtime-lab-notes.pdf.

Action items for engineering (Vivek):
- Confirm kernel selection spreadsheet covers all model families we exposed in the RFP (gpt2-like, llama variants, openclones).
- Point to the exact container tags and reproducible commands for each benchmark run.
- Produce a short Methodology appendix (1 page) describing sampling windows, traffic synthesis profile, continuous batching parameters, and KV cache measurement technique.
- If any items are sensitive (container images with proprietary hooks), flag and we'll advise on redaction or secure transfer.

Please reply with confirmation and an ETA. If you need CS or legal to sign off on any of the raw artifacts, loop them now.

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Rafael's signature

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-13 16:45 PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: runtime pipeline lab artifacts for RFP - Redwood

Rafael / Marissa,

We're ready to deliver the core artifact bundle. Attached to this message (and included in the tarball) are:
- kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx -> detailed matrix mapping model family, sequence-length buckets, chosen kernels (cuBLAS vs custom fused kernels), and rationale notes.
- runtime-benchmarks-2026-12-02.csv -> raw p50/p90/p95/p99 CSVs from controlled runs. Columns: model, batch_size, seq_len, tokens/sec, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, hw_tag.
- burnin-log-2026-12-01.tar.gz -> burn-in traces (startup timeline, cache hit rates, KV-cache warming traces).
- redwood-runtime-lab-notes.pdf -> methodology appendix (warmup policy, sampling windows, continuous-batching config, fallback rules used for graceful degradation).

Methodology summary (high level):
- Hardware: A100-80GB and Ampere-32 pools (we also include a small RTX-6000 validation run for parity).
- Load synthesis: Synthetic QPS driver with a trace-replay mode; sequence-length distribution sampled from customer corpus (median=64, 90th=256 tokens).
- Warmup: 3-minute progressive warmup ramp followed by 10-minute burn-in; we report percentiles after steady-state window (last 5 minutes).
- Batching & KV cache: Continuous batching enabled; prefix/KV cache hitrates measured by synthetic prefix-replay and reported in the burn-in traces. We include the script names used to collect these (scripts/collect_kv_metrics.sh).
- Repro commands: We include run scripts and container tags in the tarball (containers/redwood-runtime:v2026.11.9).

Security notes: raw run logs contain environment tags; we redacted ephemeral API keys. If Aperture needs private container images or full debug traces, we will provide via S3 with signed URL under the NDA.

ETA: tarball available for secure transfer now. I've uploaded to our internal staging and can provide a signed S3 link when you confirm transfer mechanism.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Performance Lead | Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx; runtime-benchmarks-2026-12-02.csv; burnin-log-2026-12-01.tar.gz; redwood-runtime-lab-notes.pdf
